text: In the twenty-second chapter of Genesis there is raised a question to which no answer is given. Abraham is bidden to take his son, his only son, whom he loves; but of Abraham's feeling nothing is told, for the narrator never looks into his inward life. He neither protests nor bargains. In this chapter he has rather the aspect of a silence than of a character, and the whole chapter turns upon that silence; no trace appears of the Abraham who pleaded for Sodom.
